name: Mizue
tagline: Tokyo in 34 minutes and Otemachi in 34 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Edogawa City, where the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 34 minutes to Otemachi, 44 minutes to Shinjuku, 52 minutes to Shibuya and 49 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 0.9 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0.4 m to 1.3 m, a difference of 0.9 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 14 clinics and 9 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 江戸川共済病院, about 11 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 江戸川共済病院, about 12 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Toei Shinjuku Line.
congestion: Toei Shinjuku Line runs at 152% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 西大島→住吉, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. 1LDK ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 2LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. quiet surroundings pushes the figure up. On the other side, a large projected flood depth and only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Mizue is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Mizue in a straight line. It is served by the same lines as Mizue. To Tokyo, for instance, Shinozaki takes 4 minutes longer. On how easy the shopping is, Mizue comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Ichinoe is ahead on how close the centre is, but Mizue is ahead on the number of medical facilities and how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Mizue in a straight line. It is served by the same lines as Mizue. To Toranomon, for instance, Ichinoe is 4 minutes quicker. A one-room flat costs about ¥5,000 more at Ichinoe. On quiet, Mizue comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 10 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Toei Shinjuku Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
